Non-browser process fan-out reading SSH/npm/Docker/AWS/browser credential stores on Arch host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Rust-based credential stealer's signature behaviour: a single short-lived process reading four or more high-value credential files (~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.aws/credentials, Chrome/Firefox cookie DBs, Slack/Discord session stores) within a short window, while excluding the legitimate browsers/CLIs that normally touch those paths. Rationale: Targets the credential-targets list directly enumerated in the article body (SSH keys, GitHub/npm/Docker/cloud tokens, browser cookies, Slack/Discord/Teams sessions). The article's stealer is Rust-compiled with an opaque process name, so the high-signal pivot is the FAN-OUT (>=4 distinct credential stores in 2 min) by a single unknown binary — that's the smoking gun a normal browser/CLI never produces.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup tools (restic, borg, duplicity) snapshotting the user's home directory — touch many credential files in quick succession
  • Dotfiles sync utilities (chezmoi, yadm) on first-run reading every config
  • Configuration management agents (ansible-pull, chef-client, puppet) re-reading host facts/agent creds
  • Endpoint AV/EDR full-disk scans reading every file — exclude by signed AV process name
  • Migration helpers like `gh auth setup-git` or `gcloud auth login` re-reading multiple credential stores in one workflow
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/lib/backup" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("restic","borg","duplicity","chezmoi","yadm","ansible","puppet-agent","chef-client","falcon-sensor","mdatp")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName + SHA256 — if SHA256 is unseen elsewhere in the org and the binary lives under /tmp, /dev/shm, ~/.cache or an AUR build dir, treat as confirmed. Capture the binary for static analysis. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, force-rotate EVERY credential the binary read (the article's IR guidance: SSH keys, GitHub/npm/cloud tokens, browser sessions, Slack/Discord/Teams). Invalidate AAD sessions for the user. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId → UC2 (was anything exfiltrated to temp.sh?) and UC4 (was eBPF persistence installed?); pivot SHA256 across the org; review pacman.log for the AUR package that introduced it.
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/glab-cli","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.config/Teams","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","ssh-agent","gpg","gpg-agent","firefox","chrome","google-chrome","chromium","brave-browser","slack","discord","teams","code","gh","glab","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault","gnome-keyring-daemon","keepassxc","keyring","snap"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpen","FileRead","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(FolderPath),
            Targets = make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            First = min(Timestamp), Last = max(Timestamp),
            Reads = count()
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, bin(Timestamp, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","gpg","firefox","chrome","chromium","slack","discord","code","gh","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Targets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR EXECVE) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_* OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.aws/credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR *cookies.sqlite OR *Cookies OR *key4.db OR *Login\ Data OR */.kube/config OR */.vault-token)) -@process.name:(ssh OR scp OR sftp OR git OR firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR slack OR discord OR code OR gh OR aws OR docker OR npm OR kubectl OR vault OR gpg OR gpg-agent OR gnome-keyring-daemon OR keepassxc)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_|known_hosts)|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|cookies\.sqlite|Cookies$|key4\.db|Login Data|\/\.config\/(Slack|discord|Teams)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.vault-token)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(ssh|scp|sftp|git|gpg|firefox|chrome|chromium|slack|discord|teams|code|gh|aws|docker|npm|kubectl|vault|gnome-keyring-daemon|keepassxc)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={ count_distinct=count(TargetFileName, distinct=true) | first_seen=min(_time) | last_seen=max(_time) })
| count_distinct >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Filesystem.file_path) as files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*cookies.sqlite*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*key4.db*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Login Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/storage*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord*") AND Filesystem.process_name!="ssh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="scp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="sftp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="git" AND Filesystem.process_name!="firefox" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chrome" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chromium" AND Filesystem.process_name!="slack" AND Filesystem.process_name!="discord" AND Filesystem.process_name!="gh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="aws" AND Filesystem.process_name!="npm" AND Filesystem.process_name!="docker" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path _time span=2m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_files >= 4 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*cookies.sqlite*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*key4.db*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Login Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/storage*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord*") AND Filesystem.process_name!="ssh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="scp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="sftp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="git" AND Filesystem.process_name!="firefox" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chrome" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chromium" AND Filesystem.process_name!="slack" AND Filesystem.process_name!="discord" AND Filesystem.process_name!="gh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="aws" AND Filesystem.process_name!="npm" AND Filesystem.process_name!="docker" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path _time span=2m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_files >= 4 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
eBPF program load or pinned object created from non-system parent on Arch host AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the article's rootkit-style persistence primitive: an eBPF program loaded or a BPF object pinned under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that isn't one of the legitimate eBPF consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd-networkd, BCC tools). Particularly noisy when paired with a recent makepkg/pacman/yay parent within the last hour. Rationale: Targets the article's explicit persistence claim — 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' (Phase 5 of the kill-chain). The clean signal is BPF objects pinned by a process that isn't a known eBPF runtime; the leftouter join to recent makepkg/pacman/yay activity raises confidence when the load happens inside an AUR build window.
ATT&CKT1014 T1547 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running ad-hoc `bcc-tools` like execsnoop, opensnoop, biotop for performance diagnostics
  • Kubernetes CNI upgrade installing a new Cilium/Calico version that hasn't refreshed its process-name list
  • Custom in-house observability agent loading eBPF probes (allowlist by SHA256)
  • Cloud-init or Ansible role provisioning Tetragon/Falco for the first time on a fresh host
  • kernel-debug session via `perf record` writing perf-event maps under /sys/fs/bpf/
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the BPF object — `bpftool prog show` and `bpftool map show` on the host (read-only); capture InitiatingProcessSHA256 and the BPF object name. If the loading process isn't a known runtime and lives under /tmp / /dev/shm / an AUR build path, treat as confirmed rootkit. 2) Contain: do NOT rely on host-resident tools (they may be hidden by the rootkit) — pull the host out of the network, image the disk from a clean rescue environment, and rebuild from trusted media per the article's IR guidance. 3) Hunt: pivot the loader SHA256 across the org; check every Arch / WSL2-Arch host for `/sys/fs/bpf/` content from non-system processes in the last 30 days; correlate with UC1 (atomic-lockfile install) on the same host.
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","systemd-resolved","bpftool","cilium-agent","cilium","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","docker","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","snap","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru")
    | project AurTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, AurFile=FileName, AurCmd=ProcessCommandLine

| extend BuildContextNearby = iif(isnotempty(AurTime) and Timestamp between (AurTime .. AurTime + 1h), true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

          BpfFile = FileName,
          Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatorParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          BuildContextNearby, AurFile, AurCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","bpftool","cilium-agent","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)

          BpfObject = TargetFilePath,

| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious eBPF Object Pinned Outside Known eBPF Consumers (Atomic Arch Rootkit)
id: 2a7c9e5d-4f3b-4c1e-8d6a-9b3c5e7f1a2c
description: Detects creation or modification of eBPF objects under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that is not one of the standard eBPF runtime consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd, BCC). Aligned with the Atomic Arch campaign's described 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' when the malware gains root.

#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^\/sys\/fs\/bpf\//
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(systemd|systemd-networkd|bpftool|cilium-agent|tetragon|falco|tracee|sysdig|containerd|runc|dockerd|kubelet|bpftrace|mdatp|falcon-sensor|perf)$/i

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as image values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/*" AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified") AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd-networkd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="bpftool" AND Filesystem.process_name!="cilium-agent" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tetragon" AND Filesystem.process_name!="falco" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tracee" AND Filesystem.process_name!="containerd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="runc" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

Persistence written to user shell init or systemd user units from AUR build/install scriptlet AIInstallation Medium
Hunts post-install persistence dropped by hijacked AUR packages — writes to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.config/systemd/user/, ~/.config/autostart/, /etc/cron.d/, or /etc/profile.d/ when the writer's parent (or grandparent) is makepkg/pacman/yay/paru/trizen/pikaur/aura. Legitimate Arch packages rarely modify the invoking user's home directory. Rationale: Combines two article-grounded signals: the persistence file locations a build-time payload would naturally use (cron/systemd/shell-rc/profile.d/ld.so.preload) AND a writer that is an AUR helper or shell carrying a PKGBUILD/.install context. Legitimate AUR packages install to /usr/... — a write to ~/.bashrc or /etc/cron.d from makepkg's child is the differentiator.
ATT&CKT1546.004 T1053.003 T1547.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Shell-framework AUR packages (oh-my-zsh-git, bash-completion variants) that DO legitimately modify ~/.zshrc/~/.bashrc by design
  • AUR packages shipping legitimate systemd units to ~/.config/systemd/user/ (rare but exists — e.g. user-mode VPN clients)
  • pacman hooks updating /etc/ld.so.cache after a library install (different from ld.so.preload but path may confuse)
  • Dotfiles-management AUR packages (chezmoi, stow) intentionally placing files in home
  • First-time provisioning runs where a fresh user account gets its initial rc files populated by an install script
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "oh-my-zsh" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "bash-completion" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "chezmoi" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "stow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the actual file content written — `cat` the persistence target and look for the malicious payload signatures (calls to /tmp/.* binaries, references to atomic-lockfile/temp.sh/fardewoak, base64-encoded blobs, ProcID hiding logic). Cross-check the source PKGBUILD against AUR upstream via `pacman -Qi` + `git log` on the AUR repo. 2) Contain: revert the persistence file to its pre-install state (or delete the rogue entry), kill any process started from it, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the AUR package name across the org to find every host that installed it; correlate with UC1/UC2/UC3 on the same DeviceId to confirm full kill-chain; remove and quarantine the package from local AUR caches.
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["/.bashrc","/.bash_profile","/.zshrc","/.profile","/.bash_aliases","/.zprofile","/.config/systemd/user/","/.config/autostart/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/systemd/system/"]);
let AurTools = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","fakeroot"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (PersistencePaths) or FileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile","ld.so.preload")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD",".install","post_install","pre_install","makepkg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          PersistenceFile = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName),
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["/.bashrc","/.bash_profile","/.zshrc","/.profile","/.config/systemd/user/","/.config/autostart/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/systemd/system/"]);
let AurTools = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","fakeroot"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (PersistencePaths) or TargetFileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile","ld.so.preload")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (AurTools)
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD",".install","post_install","pre_install","makepkg")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Writer = ActingProcessName,
          WriterCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          PersistenceFile = TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AUR Install Scriptlet Writes Persistence to User Home or System-wide Auto-Start
id: e3f1b8a6-2c5d-4a9e-b7c4-6f8d3a2e1b9f
description: Detects file writes by makepkg/pacman/yay/paru/trizen/pikaur/aura (or a child shell carrying a PKGBUILD/.install context) that land in user-shell init, systemd user units, autostart, cron, profile.d, or ld.so.preload — the persistence locations expected from the Atomic Arch hijacked AUR packages.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/400-aur-packages-hijacked-atomic-arch-campaign
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.t1546.004
  - attack.t1053.003
  - attack.t1547.013
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.bashrc'
      - '/.bash_profile'
      - '/.zshrc'
      - '/.profile'
      - '/.config/systemd/user/'
      - '/.config/autostart/'
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/etc/cron.daily/'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
      - '/etc/profile.d/'
      - '/etc/ld.so.preload'
  selection_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/makepkg'
      - '/pacman'
      - '/yay'
      - '/paru'
      - '/trizen'
      - '/pikaur'
      - '/aura'
      - '/fakeroot'
  condition: selection_path and selection_writer
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:(*/.bashrc OR */.zshrc OR */.bash_profile OR */.profile OR */.config/systemd/user/* OR */.config/autostart/* OR /etc/cron.d/* OR /etc/cron.daily/* OR /var/spool/cron/* OR /etc/profile.d/* OR /etc/ld.so.preload OR /etc/systemd/system/*) @process.name:(makepkg OR pacman OR yay OR paru OR trizen OR pikaur OR aura OR fakeroot)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\/\.bashrc|\/\.zshrc|\/\.bash_profile|\/\.profile|\/\.config\/systemd\/user\/|\/\.config\/autostart\/|\/etc\/cron\.(d|daily|hourly)\/|\/var\/spool\/cron\/|\/etc\/profile\.d\/|\/etc\/ld\.so\.preload|\/etc\/systemd\/system\/)/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|trizen|pikaur|aura|fakeroot)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process) as cmd values(Filesystem.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.bashrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_profile" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.zshrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.profile" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_aliases" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/autostart/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.daily/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.hourly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/spool/cron/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/profile.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/ld.so.preload") AND (Filesystem.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura") OR Filesystem.process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.parent_process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process) as cmd values(Filesystem.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.bashrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_profile" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.zshrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.profile" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_aliases" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/autostart/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.daily/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.hourly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/spool/cron/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/profile.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/ld.so.preload") AND (Filesystem.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura") OR Filesystem.process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.parent_process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.

Miasma/Hades known-bad SHA256 execution on developer endpoint AIInstallation Medium
Alerts when any of the 5 SHA256 hashes associated with the Miasma/Hades June 2026 campaign are observed as either an executed binary or a file written to disk on an enrolled host. Catches the worm landing or running irrespective of the delivery vector (npm install, IDE folder open, PyPI import). Rationale: Uses the 5 SHA256 IOCs pre-extracted from the StepSecurity advisory. Cross-checked against Semgrep's Miasma v2 writeup and StepSecurity's Hades campaign writeup which confirm the same hash family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/the-hades-campaign-pypi-packages • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/

  • Security researcher detonating IOC in a sandbox VM enrolled to production tenant
  • Defender threat-intel sample auto-downloaded to MpCmdRun quarantine folder

Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scans\" and FolderPath !has "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !has "\\evidence\\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the host's last 24h DeviceProcessEvents/DeviceFileEvents and confirm whether the hash was executed (process row) or only landed (file row). Identify the parent (npm.exe, node-gyp, python.exe) and the originating package/folder path. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the device in Defender (Isolate Device), force-rotate any npm/PyPI/GitHub/AWS/GCP/Azure tokens that lived on that host or in any repo the developer recently opened — assume tokens were exfiltrated. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on AccountUpn across all hosts for the same hash, then hunt UC2/UC3 (Phantom Gyp + Hades Bun) against the same user/devices to map full scope; review GitHub for any new workflow files or attacker-controlled repos.

Phantom Gyp: small binding.gyp written into node_modules during npm install AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the Miasma 'Phantom Gyp' technique: a ~157-byte binding.gyp file dropped into a package directory under node_modules that triggers code execution at the native build step of npm install, bypassing preinstall/postinstall script monitoring. Filters to package-manager parent processes so legitimate library development is not flagged. Rationale: Article explicitly names the 157-byte binding.gyp as the Phantom Gyp payload dropped during npm install. Size filter (50-500 bytes) plus the node_modules path plus the npm/yarn/pnpm parent are all article-derived; legitimate binding.gyp files in published packages are typically much larger and produced by the package author rather than dropped by tar extraction during install. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer authoring a genuinely tiny binding.gyp stub for a local native addon being tested under node_modules
  • tar.exe extracting a benign package whose author shipped a minimal binding.gyp (e.g. config-only)
  • pnpm content-addressable store unpacking many legitimate binding.gyp files during fresh install
  • Forensic analyst copying a malicious binding.gyp sample to a node_modules path for sandbox testing
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has @"\node_modules\.pnpm\@types\" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "npm publish" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "node-gyp configure"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: open the file, read its content (it will be small JS/Python embedded inside the gyp action block), and identify the package directory it landed in. Capture the package name + version from the adjacent package.json. Step 2 — Contain: kill any running node-gyp / npm install on the host, isolate the device in EDR, and force-revoke the developer's NPM_TOKEN, GitHub PAT, AWS/Azure/GCP creds, and any tokens visible in process memory of the npm invocation. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the package name across the org to identify other developers who installed the same version; trigger UC1 hash search and UC6 Bun-exfil search; query npm registry for all versions of that package published in the last 7 days.

| order by Timestamp desc

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades on-import payload: python interpreter spawns Bun runtime download AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades PyPI execution chain: an obfuscated hook in a package's __init__.py runs at import time and fetches the standalone Bun JavaScript runtime (v1.3.13/1.3.14) from GitHub releases or bun.sh, then executes the _index.js payload. Pivot is python.exe as parent of curl/wget/bun or python making outbound HTTP to Bun distribution endpoints. Rationale: Article names the Bun runtime download as the Hades execution mechanism triggered from __init__.py; corroborating writeups (Orca, SocRadar, Rescana) pin the Bun versions to 1.3.13/1.3.14 and the dropper payload filename as _index.js. python -> bun.exe is highly unusual outside this campaign because python developers virtually never bootstrap a Bun runtime. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/the-hades-campaign-pypi-packages • https://orca.security/resources/blog/hades-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.rescana.com/post/active-exploitation-alert-hades-pypi-supply-chain-attack-poisons-19-python-packages-with-bun-based-credential-stealer
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1105 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer experimentally calling out to Bun from a Python script (rare but possible for cross-runtime tooling)
  • Internal data-pipeline using a Python wrapper around a Bun script
  • Anaconda/conda-forge recipe builder fetching Bun as a build dependency
  • Sandbox/dynamic analysis tooling intentionally executing a Hades sample
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "conda-build" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Anaconda\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: enumerate the python process's recent stdin/CWD and resolve which PyPI package was imported. Pull the package's __init__.py, decode the obfuscated one-liner, and confirm Bun download URL. Capture Bun binary SHA256 and the _index.js payload. Step 2 — Contain: isolate device in Defender, kill the bun.exe process tree, force-rotate npm/GitHub/AWS/GCP/Azure/Vault/Kubernetes tokens for the affected user; revoke any SSH keys present in ~/.ssh. Pull the package version from PyPI; report to PyPI security if not already taken down. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the resolved Bun download IP/URL across all hosts (DeviceNetworkEvents); search for the _index.js payload hash; check for follow-on GitHub repo creations by the user (worm C2 channel).
let HadesPkgs = dynamic(["ensmallen","mflux-streamlit","nhmpy","ppkt2synergy","embiggen","gpsea","pyphetools"]);
// Stage A: python parent spawns bun / fetcher referencing Bun distribution
let StageA = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe")
  | where FileName in~ ("bun.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","node.exe")
  | where FileName =~ "bun.exe"
      or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","github.com/oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-darwin","bun-linux","bun-v1.3.13","bun-v1.3.14","_index.js");
// Stage B: python directly egressing to Bun distribution endpoints
let StageB = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-darwin","bun-linux")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, FileName="(network)", ProcessCommandLine="";
StageA
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP=""
| union StageB
| order by Timestamp desc
let StageA = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python(3|w)?\.exe$" or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\py\.exe$"
  | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(bun|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh|node)\.exe$"
  | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\bun\.exe$"
      or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","github.com/oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-darwin","bun-linux","bun-v1.3.13","bun-v1.3.14","_index.js")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Source="Process";
let StageB = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where SrcUsername != "" and Url has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-windows-x64","bun-darwin","bun-linux")
  | join kind=inner (ImProcessCreate | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python(3|w)?\.exe$" | project DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ProcTime=TimeGenerated, ActingProcessCommandLine) on DvcHostname
  | where TimeGenerated between (ProcTime - 5m .. ProcTime + 5m)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName="python.exe", ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName="(network)", TargetProcessCommandLine=Url, Source="Network";
StageA | union StageB | order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades PyPI Worm - Python Spawns Bun Runtime Downloader
id: 9e2f7b1c-4d6a-4f8b-b0c5-7e3d9f1a2b33
status: experimental
description: Detects python interpreter spawning a child process that downloads or invokes the Bun runtime, matching the Hades PyPI campaign's on-import payload (StepSecurity, June 2026).

Editor/AI tool auto-execute config file dropped into project tree by package manager or git AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the broader Miasma/Hades tactic of seeding editor and AI-assistant config files into a project so they execute when a developer opens the folder or starts a session. Detects writes of .vscode/tasks.json (runOn:folderOpen), .vscode/setup.mjs, .claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, or .github/setup.js when the writer is git/npm/pip/tar (not the IDE itself) — meaning the file is arriving via a clone or install, not authored locally. Rationale: The article's Table 1 enumerates exactly these 7 file paths and their auto-execute triggers. Pivoting on package-manager/git as the writer eliminates the common FP of a developer manually authoring these files in the IDE — when git clone or npm install drops them, the file came from the published package itself. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files • https://hivesecurity.gitlab.io/blog/miasma-mini-shai-hulud-ai-agent-supply-chain-2026/ • https://complexdiscovery.com/when-the-worm-targets-the-assistant-miasma-turns-ai-coding-agents-into-the-trigger/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running git clone on a legitimate repo whose maintainer ships a .vscode/tasks.json for local dev tooling
  • npm install of a package that legitimately includes a .vscode/extensions.json or task config
  • pip install of an internal dev tooling package that ships .vscode files (rare but possible)
  • yarn workspace bootstrap that copies tasks.json from a template directory
  • CI agent fetching repo with .github/setup.js used for environment setup
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/" or FolderPath has @"\internal-template-repo\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the dropped file. For tasks.json, look for runOn:folderOpen + node/bun/curl/python invocation. For setup.mjs/setup.mdc/setup.js, examine the JS for obfuscated payloads or fetches to non-corp domains. Identify the originating package (look at adjacent package.json / requirements.txt / git remote origin). Step 2 — Contain: warn the developer NOT to open the folder in VS Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini; quarantine the file; if already opened, isolate the device, kill any spawned child processes, force-rotate the developer's tokens. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the source package name across the org; run UC1 hashes, UC3 (Bun runtime), UC6 (Bun outbound) on the same host; check git log on the repo for who/when added the file.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, @"\", FileName)
| where FullPath has_any (@"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.vscode\setup.mjs", @"\.claude\setup.mjs", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
// Drop writes by the legitimate IDE — those are user authoring; keep writes by package managers / git / extractors
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","npm.exe","node.exe","pip.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","tar.exe","7z.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("git clone","git pull","git checkout","npm install","npm i ","pip install","yarn add","pnpm install")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FullPath, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.vscode\setup.mjs", @"\.claude\setup.mjs", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(git|npm|node|pip|python(3)?|yarn|pnpm|tar|7z|curl|wget|bun)\.exe$"
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("git clone","git pull","git checkout","npm install","pip install","yarn add","pnpm install")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini spawns interpreter referencing folderOpen or SessionStart hook script AIExploitation High
Detects the moment of execution for the editor/AI-tool auto-execute trigger — Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini parent-process spawning node/bun/python/powershell/cmd with a command line referencing tasks.json, setup.mjs, setup.mdc, .claude/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json, or .github/setup.js. This catches the worm running even if the dropping vector (UC4) was missed. Rationale: Article's Table 1 explicitly maps each file to its auto-execute trigger (runOn:folderOpen for tasks.json, SessionStart for .claude/setup.mjs, Custom rules load for .cursor/rules/setup.mdc). When the editor itself is the parent of an interpreter that loads one of these paths, the trigger has actually fired — much higher signal than just the file existing. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files • https://hivesecurity.gitlab.io/blog/miasma-mini-shai-hulud-ai-agent-supply-chain-2026/
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer's own .vscode/tasks.json running a legitimate build task on folder open
  • Claude Code SessionStart hook running an internal corp-approved setup.mjs
  • Cursor rules file loading a benign internal lint script
  • VS Code Remote SSH bootstrap spawning node for the remote server
  • Anaconda Python environment activation triggered by VS Code Python extension
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has @"\internal-corp-tooling\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--corp-trusted-folder")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: open the referenced setup script (setup.mjs/setup.mdc/tasks.json) and check for obfuscation, outbound fetches, or Bun runtime invocation. Identify the git remote of the project folder. Step 2 — Contain: kill the child process tree, close the IDE, isolate the device. Force-rotate npm/GitHub/AWS/GCP/Azure/Vault tokens for the developer. Step 3 — Hunt: search across the fleet for the same project path / git remote being opened by other developers. Pivot on UC6 (Bun outbound) to find post-execution exfil. Add the dropped file's SHA256 to the IOC list.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","gemini.exe","devenv.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","gemini.exe","devenv.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","bun.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc",".github\\setup.js",@"\.vscode\tasks.json",@"\.claude\settings.json",@"\.gemini\settings.json","folderOpen","SessionStart")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(code|cursor|claude|gemini|devenv)\.exe$"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(node|bun|python(3|w)?|powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|curl|wget)\.exe$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc",@"\.github\setup.js",@"\.vscode\tasks.json",@"\.claude\settings.json",@"\.gemini\settings.json","folderOpen","SessionStart")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime egress to npm/PyPI publish endpoints or attacker-controlled GitHub repos AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the Miasma/Hades worm's spreading phase: a Bun runtime instance making outbound HTTPS to npm publish, PyPI upload, or GitHub repo-creation/upload endpoints, indicating either token-driven package republishing or exfiltration to attacker-controlled GitHub repos as documented in the campaign writeup. Rationale: Article and corroborating writeups confirm the worm self-propagates by republishing infected packages (npm publish API, PyPI upload API) using stolen tokens, and exfiltrates harvested credentials through attacker-controlled GitHub repos. bun.exe contacting these endpoints from a developer endpoint (not a CI runner) is high-signal because developers rarely use Bun to drive npm/PyPI/GitHub APIs interactively. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/the-hades-campaign-pypi-packages • https://orca.security/resources/blog/hades-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567 T1059.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately experimenting with Bun + npm publish for a personal package
  • Bun-based CI tool running publish in a non-CI dev environment
  • Node.js developer using a bun-runtime project that calls GitHub API for legitimate repo management
  • Renovate-bot-style tooling running under node.exe that touches api.github.com/repos
  • Engineer pushing a code snippet to a personal GitHub gist via a Bun script
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Bun\" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "renovate"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the bun.exe folder path (was it dropped under %TEMP%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, or a project node_modules?), pull its SHA256 and the parent process. If parent is python.exe or a folderOpen-spawned node, treat as confirmed Hades/Miasma. Step 2 — Contain: block the destination URL at the proxy/EDR network containment, isolate the device, revoke ALL of the developer's npm, PyPI, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes tokens — the article specifies these are the harvested targets. Audit GitHub for any repos created by the developer's PAT in the last 24h (worm exfil channel). Step 3 — Hunt: check the npm/PyPI registry for any package versions published by the developer's accounts in the suspect window; treat any such publication as a worm-spread event and request takedown. Run UC1, UC3, UC5 across the fleet for the same user.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun.exe","node.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish","registry.npmjs.org/-/user","upload.pypi.org/legacy","api.github.com/user/repos","api.github.com/repos","api.github.com/gists")
   or (RemoteUrl has "api.github.com" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("_index.js","bun-","setup.mjs"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Url has_any ("registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish","registry.npmjs.org/-/user","upload.pypi.org/legacy","api.github.com/user/repos","api.github.com/repos","api.github.com/gists")
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(bun|node)\.exe$"
    | project DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ProcTime=TimeGenerated
  ) on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (ProcTime - 30m .. ProcTime + 30m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 2f8c5a7d-9b3e-4c1f-a5d8-7e4f9b2c3d66
status: experimental
description: Detects bun.exe (or node.exe carrying the Bun payload) making outbound HTTPS to npm publish, PyPI upload, or GitHub repo/gist creation endpoints — the Miasma/Hades worm spreading and exfiltration channels.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  dest:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'registry.npmjs.org'
      - 'upload.pypi.org'
      - 'api.github.com'
  condition: proc and dest
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\BUN.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) @DestinationHostname:(registry.npmjs.org OR upload.pypi.org OR api.github.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(bun|node)\.exe$/i
| DomainName=/^(registry\.npmjs\.org|upload\.pypi\.org|api\.github\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| count>0
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(All_Traffic.url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe" AND (All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish*" OR All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/user*" OR All_Traffic.url="*upload.pypi.org/legacy/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/user/repos*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/contents/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/git/refs*") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Traffic.url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe" AND (All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish*" OR All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/user*" OR All_Traffic.url="*upload.pypi.org/legacy/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/user/repos*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/contents/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/git/refs*") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'

falsepositives:

level: critical

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution

Medium

Rust Clipboard Hijacker Uses Fake GitHub Stars and VirusTotal Upvotes to Steal Crypto

Cyber Security News
2026-06-18 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

A newly discovered malware campaign is quietly draining cryptocurrency wallets by doing something most security tools never see coming. Instead of relying on brute-force attacks or dark web exploits, the threat actor behind this campaign built a fake reputation engine across multiple platforms to make dangerous software look completely safe and trustworthy. The malware at [&#8230;] The post Rust Clipboard Hijacker Uses Fake GitHub Stars and VirusTotal Upvotes to Steal Crypto appeared first on Cyber Security News .

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — From package to postinstall payload: Inside the Mastra npm supply chain compromi
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mastra npm supply chain: easy-day-js postinstall dropper (node setup.cjs --no-warnings) · [LLM] Mastra implant Windows persistence: NvmProtocal Run key + NodePackages drop · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Mastra C2 beacon: node.exe to Hostwinds 23.254.164.92:8000 / .123:443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mastra implant credential access: node.exe reading crypto wallet extensions / browser History · [LLM] Mastra implant discovery: PowerShell child of node.exe running Get-StartApps / Get-AppxPackage · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Mastra npm supply chain: easy-day-js postinstall dropper (node setup.cjs --no-warnings) AIInstallation High
Detects the easy-day-js@1.11.22 postinstall hook spawning the obfuscated setup.cjs dropper via Node.js with the --no-warnings flag. This is the entry point execution on any developer workstation or CI/CD runner that resolved the poisoned mastra/@mastra packages. Rationale: Anchors on the exact strings published by Microsoft for the malicious postinstall — node binary spawning setup.cjs with --no-warnings (Block 1 of the article). Also restricts the parent to npm/node/yarn/pnpm lineage to slash FPs from unrelated scripts that share the filename. Cross-referenced the mastra GitHub issue 18046 which confirms the postinstall hook in easy-day-js@1.11.22. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046 • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/microsoft-threat-intelligence_microsoft-has-identified-a-supply-chain-attack-activity
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal npm package whose postinstall is also named setup.cjs and invokes node --no-warnings (rare — the dual-string match makes this unlikely)
  • Developer manually testing/reverse-engineering the malicious dropper after the campaign was disclosed
  • A CI/CD job that intentionally runs a script literally called setup.cjs with warnings suppressed
  • Security tooling (EDR sandbox, npm audit replays) that re-executes the dropper for analysis
Suppression filter
| where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4","c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638","cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066","9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9","221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or FolderPath has @"\node_modules\easy-day-js\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree on the host (parent npm/yarn → node setup.cjs); collect the SHA256 of the setup.cjs file and compare to the five published hashes; check $TMPDIR for .pkg_history and .pkg_logs markers. 2) Contain: isolate the host or CI runner from network, kill node tree, quarantine node_modules/easy-day-js, rotate every credential / token / SSH key / cloud key that touched that machine since 2026-06-16 07:05 UTC. 3) Hunt: query all hosts that ran npm install/update against the mastra or @mastra scope or that resolved easy-day-js@1.11.21 or 1.11.22 between 2026-06-16 and 2026-06-17; pivot to UC2/UC3/UC5 to confirm second-stage and persistence.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "setup.cjs" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\easy-day-js\", "easy-day-js/setup.cjs")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has "setup.cjs" and CommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mastra npm Supply Chain easy-day-js Postinstall Dropper
id: a1f8c3d4-7b2e-4f9a-8c5d-1e6b9f2a3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the easy-day-js@1.11.22 postinstall hook spawning the obfuscated setup.cjs dropper via Node.js with --no-warnings.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
  - https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046
author: ThreatHunting-Now
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1546.016
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\node.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'setup.cjs'
      - '--no-warnings'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Benign npm packages whose postinstall happens to be named setup.cjs and invoke node with --no-warnings (uncommon)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR */node) OR @process.executable.path:(*\\node.exe OR */node)) (@CommandLine:(*setup.cjs* AND *--no-warnings*) OR @process.command_line:(*setup.cjs* AND *--no-warnings*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$|\/node$/i CommandLine=/setup\.cjs/i CommandLine=/--no-warnings/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
